messages:
Alex: Night bridge here — I'm primary until 07:00 PT. Maya is my secondary. Heads-up: we're seeing an uptick in 99th latency for hosted/text-gen in us-west (started ~20m ago). I'll be swapping primary at 02:00 PT; there's a brief coverage gap ~02:00-02:20 PT while I handoff. Leaving quick runbook pointers below.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: latency-api/us-west > 99th percentile for 5m. auto-escalation: P2. Pages sent to on-call. Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/1939991234

Maya: ack, I'm on standby for the swap window. Quick question — what should I do first if the 99th stays high after the usual restarts?

Alex: good q. Prioritized checklist (short):
1) Confirm customer impact (are requests timing out or just slower?). If HTTP 5xx increase -> escalate.
2) Check KV cache hit rate for the model (prefix cache). If hit rate < 60% => warm caches.
3) Look at Dedicated pool utilization and queued requests. If GPUs are saturated, scale or failover to smaller model variant.
4) If memory OOMs on runtime, roll a targeted restart of the offending worker pool.

Jon: adding concrete ops commands:
```bash
# Check top latency traces in tracing UI
open https://console.redwood.dev/traces?service=serving-runtime&filter=us-west

# Flush prefix cache for a specific model (use cautiously)
redwoodctl cache flush --model "redwood-v1-13b" --prefix "session-abc"

# Restart worker pool in us-west (graceful)
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/worker-pool-usw-1
```

Sam: if Dedicated pool is near 100% util, quick mitigation: scale a burst pool or route a portion of traffic to fallback model. Example command (internal):
```
/scale-pool --pool dedicated-usw-2 --delta 2 --reason "night latency spike"
/route-policy apply --route latency-experiment --percent 20 --model redwood-v1-7b-quant
```

Tia: customer impact update — looked at metrics: only hosted customers in us-west are affected; dedicated tenants and private deployments are fine. If we route 30% of traffic to a smaller variant we should see 99th drop within 2–5m. Also warn SREs to watch cost delta.

Maya: thanks. For the handoff: I'll follow these runbook steps if page persists. Also please paste direct links to the runbooks so I don't have to hunt.

ops-bot: Runbooks & quick links — (bookmark these)
- Latency triage: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/latency-triage
- KV cache / hot-prefixes: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/kv-cache
- Worker pool restart: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/worker-pool-restart
- Model fallback & routing: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/model-fallback

Alex: copy-paste checklist I leave for Maya during the swap:
- Before swap: announce handoff in #eng-oncall and confirm secondary ack (done).
- If page happens during swap: secondary takes alert routing; primary stands by for escalation.
- First 5m: validate scope (region, model, tenant).
- 5–15m: apply short-term mitigations (route 20–30% to fallback, scale burst pool).
- 15–45m: if degradation persists, escalate to on-call SREs and open incident document.

Maya: I got it. I'll watch traces and apply the 20% fallback if 99th stays > baseline for 10m.

Jon: small note — when flushing prefix cache, do NOT run for global prefixes. Use single-session prefixes only. I've added the TTL guidance in the KV runbook.

Sam: if we do scale, ping me and I'll verify autoscaler logs.

Alex: leaving one more tip — prefer routing policy changes over immediate restarts when traffic is heavy; restarts can cause transient 5xxs. Use restarts as targeted last-resort on bad worker IDs.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: scheduled: handoff reminder at 02:00 PT posted to channel.

Tia: customer comms note — if we open an incident, include impacted tenants list and estimated duration; keep status updates every 30m.

Alex: ok i'm swapping to secondary now. Maya, you're primary. I'm reachable via DMs if you need me. Leaving quick quick-links here again for the swap window: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/latency-triage | https://runbooks.redwood.internal/kv-cache | https://runbooks.redwood.internal/model-fallback :thumbsup:

Maya: taking over now. thanks Alex. I'll post any pages and start with the tracing link.

incident-bot: Update: latency-api/us-west 99th still elevated at +12% after 10m.

Maya: applying 20% routing to redwood-v1-7b-quant now (/route-policy apply). Will monitor 5m windows and report back.

Alex: thanks — great handoff. Leaving this thread open for updates; will close once metrics stabilize for 30m. :handshake:
